sections.heading: Ambedkar — the arc of a liberation

blocks.text: **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (14 April 1891, Mhow – 6 December 1956)**: born Mahar, educated at Columbia (PhD; Dewey's pragmatism) and LSE (DSc; Gray's Inn bar) — the most formally educated founder, whose life ran from being denied classroom water to authoring the Constitution's promise of equality. Method: **educate, agitate, organise** — institutions before emotion, law as liberation's instrument.

rows: Awakening (1919-27)
Southborough testimony (1919); **Mooknayak (1920)**; **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)**; **Mahad Satyagraha (Mar 1927** — Chavadar tank water; **Manusmriti burnt 25 Dec 1927**)
Civil-rights method: claim public goods, burn the ideology; 'we will not be satisfied with chappals' equality of appearance
Temple-entry & politics (1927-36)

**Kalaram Temple satyagraha (Nashik, 1930-35)**; RTC delegate (all three); **Communal Award → Poona Pact (1932)**; *Annihilation of Caste* (1936 — the undelivered Jat-Pat-Todak address); **Independent Labour Party (1936)**
Concluded temple-entry insufficient — power, not permission; ILP fused caste with class (mill workers, khoti tenants)
Statecraft (1937-46)
Bombay Assembly; **Viceroy's Executive Council — Labour Member (1942-46)**; **Scheduled Castes Federation (1942)**; *What Congress and Gandhi Have Done…*, *Who Were the Shudras?*
Labour laws (8-hour day discussions, ESI groundwork), water-power policy (Damodar/CWC seeds) — the administrator Ambedkar
Constitution (1946-51)
Constituent Assembly (Bengal, then Bombay); **Drafting Committee Chairman (29 Aug 1947)**; Law Minister; **Hindu Code Bill** fight → resignation (Sept 1951)

Arts 14-17 (equality, untouchability abolished), 25(2)(b) temple entry, reservations architecture, Art 32 ('the soul'); constitutional morality; 'grammar of anarchy' & the 20 Nov 1955? — his warnings speech **25 Nov 1949**
Renunciation (1951-56)
**Buddhist conversion, Nagpur, 14 October 1956** (~5 lakh followers); *The Buddha and His Dhamma*; People's Education Society (Siddharth, Milind colleges)
Exit from caste's cosmos — dhamma as social equality; the Navayana legacy

sections.heading: Ideas that outlived him — and the AP thread

items: **Against village romance**: 'the village is a sink of localism, a den of ignorance' — his urban-constitutional route contrasts Gandhi's village-centrism: the classic comparison.

**Democracy as social**: 'Political democracy cannot last unless there lies at the base of it social democracy' — liberty-equality-fraternity as a **union of trinity**; fraternity his deepest category.

**Economics**: *The Problem of the Rupee* (RBI's conceptual pre-history); state socialism in *States and Minorities* (1947); land nationalisation advocacy — the economist Ambedkar the exam under-asks but rewards.
**Warnings (25 Nov 1949)**: bhakti in politics 'a sure road to degradation'; contradictions of political equality amid social inequality — quote-ready for essays.

**AP thread**: Ambedkar's mass following in coastal Andhra (Dalit movements of Krishna-Guntur), the **Adi-Andhra movement (1917 Vijayawada conference lineage — Bhagya Reddy Varma's influence)**; AP later named its university (**Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University, Srikakulam**), Konaseema district after him (2022), and raised the **125-ft 'Statue of Social Justice' (Vijayawada, 2024)** — the state's institutional homage; his constitutional machinery (SC reservations, Art 371D's equity logic) governs AP daily.

blocks.text: Exam tip: One Ambedkar quote per answer, precisely attributed — the 25 Nov 1949 speech is the safest source. The AP homage set (university, district, Statue of Social Justice) is the regional close examiners now expect.

prelimsPointers: **Mahad Satyagraha: 20 March 1927** (Chavadar tank); **Manusmriti dahan: 25 December 1927**.
**Kalaram temple satyagraha: Nashik, 2 March 1930** (with Sane Guruji-era volunteers).
Journals: **Mooknayak (1920), Bahishkrit Bharat (1927), Janata, Prabuddha Bharat**.
**Annihilation of Caste (1936)** — rejected address to Jat-Pat-Todak Mandal, Lahore.
**Drafting Committee chairman from 29 August 1947** (7 members); Law Minister 1947-51; resigned over the **Hindu Code Bill (1951)**.
**Conversion: Nagpur (Deekshabhoomi), 14 October 1956**; died **6 December 1956 (Mahaparinirvan Diwas)**; Bharat Ratna **1990**.
*The Problem of the Rupee* (1923) fed the **Hilton Young Commission** groundwork before RBI (1935).
AP homages: **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district (2022)**; **125-ft Statue of Social Justice, Vijayawada (inaugurated 2024)**.
mainsAngles: Educate, agitate, organise — periodise Ambedkar's movement from Mahad to the Constitution.
Ambedkar sought power, not permission — analyse his shift from temple entry to political safeguards.
Compare Gandhi and Ambedkar on caste, village and method, marking both conflict and convergence.
Political democracy without social democracy is a palace on dung — expound Ambedkar's 25 November 1949 warnings for today.
Assess Ambedkar the economist and administrator — rupee, labour and water — beyond the constitutionalist.

glossary.definition: Ambedkar's 1924 organisation for the outcastes' education and civil rights — motto: educate, agitate, organise.
The 1927 assertion of untouchables' right to public water at Chavadar tank — India's founding Dalit civil-rights action.
Ambedkar's 1936 text arguing caste cannot be reformed, only annihilated — with shastra-authority itself the target.
Ambedkar's 1942 political party for Dalit self-representation — predecessor of the Republican Party of India.
Ambedkar's socially-engaged rereading of Buddhism — the 1956 conversion's 'new vehicle' of equality and rationality.
Ambedkar's demand for allegiance to constitutional forms and restraint — 'not a natural sentiment; it has to be cultivated'.

sections.heading: The struggle in three acts — the synthesis note

blocks.text: This theme asks for the **periodised whole**: **1885-1905 (Moderate)** — constitutional persuasion, economic critique; **1905-1920 (Extremist-revolutionary)** — swadeshi mass techniques, revolutionary terrorism's first wave, Home Rule's bridge; **1920-1947 (Gandhian)** — three mass waves (NCM 1920-22, CDM 1930-34, QIM 1942) alternating with constitutional engagement (Swarajists, 1937 office) and flanked by revolutionaries (HSRA), leftists (CSP, CPI), Ambedkarite and Periyarist social struggles, and Bose's armed finale. The craft is **characterising each phase's method-social base-achievement-limit in two lines**, then the connective tissue: each phase inherited the last's cadre and corrected its failure.

rows: Petition, press, drain critique; lawyers-journalists elite
Nation imagined, 1892 Act, economic nationalism / mass distance, British deafness

Boycott-swadeshi, national education, passive resistance; students, urban middle class; revolutionary cells (Anushilan, Ghadar 1913, Komagata Maru 1914); Lucknow Pact (1916 — Congress-League, separate electorates conceded); Home Rule's membership politics
Mass techniques invented, Bengal reunited (1911), Montagu promise (1917) / communal electorates seeded (1909), repression-lull cycles

Gandhian satyagraha cycles + constructive programme + negotiation; peasants-workers-women-students; parallel streams — HSRA (Bhagat Singh's socialist turn; Assembly bomb 1929, Lahore conspiracy), left (Meerut case 1929, CSP 1934), princely-state praja mandals, Ambedkar-Periyar social democracy, INA climax
Ungovernability proven, army shaken, power transferred / Partition's price; social-question deferred (the unfinished revolution)

sections.heading: Threads across phases — and Andhra's presence in each

items: **Continuity threads**: economic critique (Naoroji→khadi→planning committee 1938); communal question (1909 electorates→1916 Lucknow→1932 Award→1940 Lahore resolution→1947); the state's repressive learning curve (1878 acts→Rowlatt→1932 ordinances); women's ascent (Swadeshi's rakhi→Dharasana pickets→1942 leadership: Aruna, Usha, Matangini, Durgabai).

**Gandhi's distinct additions**: mass discipline (satyagraha's rules), constructive programme (khadi-untouchability-unity as politics between storms), negotiation-readiness (Pacts as strategy, not weakness), and the **movement-truce-movement rhythm** that trained rather than exhausted the nation (Bipan Chandra's 'struggle-truce-struggle').

**Andhra in each phase**: Moderate era — Ananda Charlu, the Madras sessions; Extremist era — Rajahmundry Vandemataram militancy, Gadicherla's *Swarajya*; Gandhian era — Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu, Alluri's Rampa (1922-24), Mypadu salt, Quit India's Tenali; and throughout, the **parallel Andhra movement** for linguistic identity (Andhra Mahasabhas from 1913) braided with nationalism — the region fought for India and for Andhra simultaneously (HCOA notes complete this).

**Verdict**: freedom came from **compounded pressures** — mass movements' ungovernability + war exhaustion + army unreliability (INA/RIN) + international delegitimation — no single-cause answer survives scrutiny.

blocks.text: Exam tip: When the question spans 1885-1947, examiners grade the ARCHITECTURE of your answer — phases characterised, threads connected, verdict argued. Resist the chronicle; write the analysis.

prelimsPointers: Phase markers: **1892 Councils Act; 1905 partition; 1907 Surat; 1916 Lucknow Pact & Home Rule; 1920 Nagpur; 1929 Purna Swaraj; 1935 Act; 1942 Quit India; 1946 Cabinet Mission**.
**Ghadar Party: 1913, San Francisco (Lala Har Dayal)**; **Komagata Maru: 1914**.
**HSRA (1928, Delhi — Chandrashekhar Azad)**; Saunders shooting (1928), **Assembly bomb 8 April 1929**, Lahore conspiracy executions **23 March 1931**.
**Lucknow Pact 1916**: Congress-League joint scheme; Congress accepted separate electorates.
**Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929-33)**; **Congress Socialist Party 1934 (JP, Lohia, Narendra Dev)**.
**National Planning Committee 1938 (Bose's presidency; Nehru chair)** — economic nationalism institutionalised.
Andhra thread markers: **Andhra PCC (1918 — among the first linguistic PCCs)**; Alluri's Rampa **1922-24**.

The Gandhian rhythm of struggle-truce-struggle trained a nation — evaluate Bipan Chandra's framework.
Mainstream and margins — integrate the revolutionaries, the left and the social-justice streams into the national narrative.
1947 had many authors — argue the compounded-pressures explanation of the transfer of power.
Andhra fought two freedoms at once — trace the braiding of nationalism and Andhra identity across the three phases.

glossary.definition: Bipan Chandra's characterisation of Gandhian strategy — mass phases alternating with constructive/negotiation phases to sustain capacity.
Khadi, untouchability removal, communal unity, village work — Gandhian politics between movements; the nation built while resting.
Armed underground actions (Anushilan, Ghadar, HSRA) — the parallel stream whose socialist maturation was Bhagat Singh.
People's associations in princely states linking their struggles to the national movement (AISPC, 1927).
Communal voting introduced in 1909, conceded at Lucknow 1916, expanded 1932 — the institutional groove toward Partition.
The 1945-47 endgame — elections, Cabinet Mission, interim government, Mountbatten Plan — by which Britain exited a compounding crisis.

rows: **Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto)**
Councils enlarged; first Indian in Executive Council (**Satyendra Sinha**); indirect elections; **separate electorates for Muslims** (Simla deputation 1906's harvest)
'Constitutional' communalism institutionalised — the fatal groove; reform as counter-insurgency after Swadeshi
**GoI Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford)**

**Dyarchy in provinces** (transferred: education, health, local govt — Indian ministers; reserved: police, revenue — executive councillors); bicameral centre; direct elections (~10% franchise); **separate electorates extended** (Sikhs etc.); Public Service Commission promised; **10-year review clause** (hence Simon)
Responsibility without power — ministers sans purse; centre untouched; yet the first responsible-government germ and legislative apprenticeship
**GoI Act 1935**

**All-India Federation** (never born — princes' accession threshold unmet); **provincial autonomy** (dyarchy abolished in provinces — popular ministries 1937); **dyarchy moved to the centre**; separate electorates persisted + Poona-Pact seats; **federal court (1937), RBI (1935)**, Burma separated, Sindh & Orissa created; franchise ~14%; **safeguards & special responsibilities** (Governors' veto powers)

'A machine with strong brakes and no engine' (Nehru: 'new charter of slavery'; Jinnah: 'thoroughly rotten'); yet independent India's **administrative skeleton** — the 1950 Constitution's largest single source

sections.heading: Commissions & missions — Simon to Cabinet Mission

items: **Simon Commission (1927-30)**: all-white statutory review (the 1919 Act's clause, advanced by two years) → universal boycott, Lala Lajpat Rai's death; its report (federation, dyarchy's end) fed the RTCs — remembered for the insult more than the text; counter-product: the **Nehru Report (1928)**, India's first swadeshi constitution draft (dominion status, rights, joint electorates) and Jinnah's **Fourteen Points (1929)** — the parting of ways.

**Cripps Mission (March 1942)**: war-pressed offer — post-war **dominion status**, constitution-making body, **provincial opt-out** (Pakistan's seed acknowledged) — rejected by all (Congress: 'post-dated cheque'; League: no explicit Pakistan); its failure precipitated Quit India.

**Cabinet Mission (March-June 1946)**: the last unity design — **no Pakistan; three-tier federation with Groups A/B/C**; centre limited to defence-foreign affairs-communications; Constituent Assembly (elected July 1946); interim government (Sept 1946, Nehru). Wrecked on **grouping's interpretation** (compulsory vs optional), Jinnah's withdrawal → **Direct Action Day (16 Aug 1946**, Calcutta killings) → the slide to **Mountbatten's 3 June Plan** and the **Indian Independence Act 1947**.

**The connective judgment**: each instrument offered **too little, too late, too divided** — 1909's electorates, 1919's dyarchy, 1935's brakes, 1942's post-dating, 1946's grouping — constitutionalism kept pace with neither nationalism's demands nor communalism's growth; yet cumulatively they built the **institutional India** (elections, legislatures, federal court, RBI, services) that 1950 constitutionalised.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Examiners love 'evaluate the 1935 Act' — answer with the paradox: the nationalists' 'charter of slavery' became the republic's chassis. Cabinet Mission questions turn on the grouping clause; state it precisely.

prelimsPointers: **1909**: separate Muslim electorates; **Satyendra P. Sinha** first Indian in the Viceroy's Executive Council.
**1919**: **dyarchy** (transferred vs reserved subjects) in provinces; bicameral central legislature; **statutory review after 10 years**.

**1935**: provincial autonomy; **federation conditional on princely accession (≥50% states' population) — never met**; **dyarchy at the centre**; Burma separated (1937); **Sindh & Orissa created (1936)**; Federal Court **1 Oct 1937**.
Nehru: 1935 Act a **'new charter of slavery'**; the phrase 'machine with strong brakes but no engine' is also quoted of it.
**Cripps (Mar-Apr 1942)**: dominion status post-war + provincial opt-out; 'post-dated cheque'.
**Cabinet Mission (1946)**: members **Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, A.V. Alexander**; **Groups A, B, C**; rejected Pakistan; CA elections July 1946; **Direct Action Day 16 Aug 1946**.
**Nehru Report 1928** (Motilal; dominion, fundamental rights, joint electorates) vs **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)**.
**Indian Independence Act: 18 July 1947**; appointed day 15 August 1947.
mainsAngles: Trace the constitutional ladder of 1909-1919-1935 as reform, containment and groove-cutting at once.
Dyarchy gave responsibility without power — dissect the 1919 experiment and its pedagogic by-products.
The 1935 Act was denounced by nationalists and inherited by the republic — resolve the paradox.
Why did the Cabinet Mission, the last design for a united India, fail? Weigh grouping, trust and Direct Action.
From Simon to Mountbatten, British constitutionalism was always a step behind Indian nationalism — evaluate.

glossary.definition: The 1919 division of provincial subjects into transferred (Indian ministers) and reserved (executive councillors) — dual government by design.
The 1935 Act's grant of fully responsible government in provinces — realised in the 1937 ministries.
The 1935 all-India federation conditional on princely accession — the engine that never started.
Governors' and Viceroy's special powers and vetoes in the 1935 Act — the 'strong brakes' on elected engines.
The Cabinet Mission's clustering of provinces into sections A, B, C for constitution-making — its compulsory/optional ambiguity killed the plan.
The League's 16 August 1946 mass action — Calcutta's killings opening the partition spiral.
